title: Fitting magnetization dynamics
text: magnetization direction \(\mathbf m\), \(|\mathbf m| = 1\), follows Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation Landau-Lifshitz form \[ \dot{\mathbf m} = -\frac{\gamma}{1+\alpha^2} \left[\mathbf m\times\mathbf h + \alpha\,\mathbf m\times(\mathbf m\times\mathbf h)\right], \qquad \gamma = \frac{g\,\mu_B}{\hbar}, \] Gilbert damping \(\alpha\) g-factor \(g\). effective field applied field, tilted \(\phi\) normal \(\hat{\mathbf z}\), plus anisotropy field \(H_a\): \[ \mathbf h = H\,(\sin\phi,\,0,\,\cos\phi) + H_a\,\bigl(1 - k(t)\bigr)\,m_z\,\hat{\mathbf z}. \] Heating lowers \(H_a\) \(k(t) = K\,\kappa(t)\), \(\kappa(0) = 1\), \(\dot\kappa = -\kappa/\tau_K\). pump, \(\mathbf m\) rests zero-torque direction \(\mathbf m_0 = (\sin\theta_0, 0, \cos\theta_0)\), \[ H\sin(\theta_0-\phi) + H_a\sin\theta_0\cos\theta_0 = 0 , \] \(\mathbf h(\mathbf m_0) = \lambda\,\mathbf m_0\), \(\lambda = H\cos(\theta_0-\phi) + H_a\cos^2\theta_0\). drop \(H_a\) moves equilibrium; \(\mathbf m\) precesses \(H_a\) recovers. states \(\boldsymbol\xi = (\mathbf m - \mathbf m_0)/K\) \(\kappa\). Since \(\mathbf m_0\times\mathbf h(\mathbf m_0) = 0\), right-hand side polynomial \(K\) without constant term: exact \(K\), linearized \(K\0\), free cancellation \(m_{z0} - m_z\).
code: muB <- 8.794e-5                      # mu_B / hbar in rad / (ps mT)  a   <- "(10^log10Alpha)"                                  # positive parameters as log10 g   <- sprintf("(%g*10^log10G/(1 + %s^2))", muB, a) xm  <- "(xi_x*sin(th) + xi_z*cos(th))"                  # xi . m0 xx  <- "(xi_x^2 + xi_y^2 + xi_z^2)"                     # xi . xi eta <- "(10^log10Ha*(xi_z - kap*(cos(th) + K*xi_z)))"   # (h - lam m0) / K, z a1  <- sprintf("(lam*%s + %s*cos(th))", xm, eta) a2  <- sprintf("(%s*xi_z)", eta) b1  <- sprintf("(2*%s)", xm) b2  <- xx  # m x h / K cx <- sprintf("(lam*xi_y*cos(th) + K*%s*xi_y)", eta) cy <- sprintf("(lam*(xi_z*sin(th) - xi_x*cos(th)) - %s*sin(th) - K*%s*xi_x)",               eta, eta) cz <- "(-lam*xi_y*sin(th))"  # (m (m.h) - h (m.m)) / K dx <- sprintf(paste0("(lam*xi_x + sin(th)*%s - lam*sin(th)*%s",                      " + K*(xi_x*%s + sin(th)*%s - lam*sin(th)*%s)",                      " + K^2*xi_x*%s)"),               a1, b1, a1, a2, b2, a2) dy <- sprintf("(lam*xi_y + K*xi_y*%s + K^2*xi_y*%s)", a1, a2) dz <- sprintf(paste0("(lam*xi_z + cos(th)*%s - %s - lam*cos(th)*%s",                      " + K*(xi_z*%s + cos(th)*%s - %s*%s - lam*cos(th)*%s)",                      " + K^2*(xi_z*%s - %s*%s))"),               a1, eta, b1, a1, a2, eta, b1, b2, a2, eta, b2)  llg <- c(   xi_x = sprintf("-%s*(%s + %s*%s)", g, cx, a, dx),   xi_y = sprintf("-%s*(%s + %s*%s)", g, cy, a, dy),   xi_z = sprintf("-%s*(%s + %s*%s)", g, cz, a, dz),   kap  = "-kap*10^(-log10TauK)" )  # Initial states xi = 0 and kappa = 1 are not estimated. H and phi enter only # through th and lam. model <- cppODE(llg, fixed = c("xi_x", "xi_y", "xi_z", "kap"),                 modelname = "copt_precession", method = "bdf", deriv = TRUE)

title: Fitting magnetization dynamics
text: anomalous Hall conductivity proportional --plane magnetization; two exponentials per measurement describe demagnetization recovery: \[ y(t) = A_1 e^{-t/\tau_1} + A_2 e^{-t/\tau_2} + S\,\bigl[m_{z0} - m_z(t)\bigr]      = A_1 e^{-t/\tau_1} + A_2 e^{-t/\tau_2} - S\,K\,\xi_z(t). \] Shared fields: \(\alpha\), \(g\), \(H_a\), \(\tau_K\), \(S\), \(K\), \(\phi\). Per measurement: background noise level. \(H\) set field, \(\mu_B/\hbar\) fixed constant. cppDE returns \(\partial\boldsymbol\xi/\partial p\); \(\theta_0\) \(\lambda\) depend \(H_a\) \(\phi\) implicit function theorem, \[ \frac{\partial\theta_0}{\partial H_a} = -\frac{\sin\theta_0\cos\theta_0}{D},\qquad \frac{\partial\theta_0}{\partial\phi} = \frac{H\cos(\theta_0-\phi)}{D},\qquad D = H\cos(\theta_0-\phi) + H_a\cos 2\theta_0 , \] chain rule completes sensitivities \(H_a\) \(\phi\). residual autocorrelation decays within five samples (one picosecond), noise moving average [2], \[ u_t = \eta_t + \sum_{j=1}^{5} w_j\,\eta_{t-j},\qquad \eta_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2), \] shared kernel \(w\) \(\sigma\) per measurement. Without correlation beyond five samples, noise model absorb precession. likelihood, conditional sum squares innovations \(\eta_t\) \(\log\sigma\) pseudo-residual, stays least squares. Ljung-Box test [3] checks innovations remaining correlation.
code: equilibrium <- function(Ha, H, phi) {   torque <- function(th) H * sin(th - phi) + Ha * sin(th) * cos(th)   th     <- uniroot(torque, c(0, phi), tol = 1e-12 * phi)$root   sc     <- sin(th) * cos(th)   den    <- H * cos(th - phi) + Ha * cos(2 * th)   thHa   <- -sc / den   thPhi  <- H * cos(th - phi) / den   list(theta = th,        lam   = H * cos(th - phi) + Ha * cos(th)^2,        dHa   = c(th = thHa,  lam = cos(th)^2 - Ha * sc * thHa),        dPhi  = c(th = thPhi, lam = H * sin(th - phi) - Ha * sc * thPhi)) }  physics   <- c("log10Alpha", "log10G", "log10Ha", "log10TauK", "log10S",                "logit10K", "logit10Phi") kernel    <- paste0("w", 1:5) bgNames   <- function(f) paste0(c("log10A1_", "log10Tau1_", "log10A2_",                                   "log10Tau2_"), f) sigmaName <- function(f) paste0("logSigma_", f) ln10      <- log(10)  traceSignal <- function(p, k, tt) {   H   <- 100 * fields[k]   bn  <- bgNames(fields[k])   K   <- toNatural("logit10K", p[["logit10K"]])   S   <- 10^p[["log10S"]]   Ha  <- 10^p[["log10Ha"]]   u   <- toNatural("logit10Phi", p[["logit10Phi"]])   phi <- pi / 2 * u                          # between 0 and 90 degrees   eqm <- equilibrium(Ha, H, phi)   pars <- c(xi_x = 0, xi_y = 0, xi_z = 0, kap = 1, K = K, th = eqm$theta,             lam = eqm$lam, p[c("log10Alpha", "log10G", "log10Ha", "log10TauK")])   sol <- tryCatch(solveODE(model, c(0, tt), pars, abstol = 1e-9, reltol = 1e-9),                   error = function(e) NULL)   if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)    xi      <- sol$variable[-1, "xi_z"]   dxi     <- sol$tangent[-1, "xi_z", , drop = TRUE]   viaRest <- function(d) dxi[, "th"] * d[["th"]] + dxi[, "lam"] * d[["lam"]]   prec    <- -S * K * xi   T1 <- 10^p[[bn[2]]]   T2 <- 10^p[[bn[4]]]   e1 <- 10^p[[bn[1]]] * exp(-tt / T1)   e2 <- 10^p[[bn[3]]] * exp(-tt / T2)    J <- matrix(0, length(tt), length(p), dimnames = list(NULL, names(p)))   J[, "log10Alpha"] <- -S * K * dxi[, "log10Alpha"]   J[, "log10G"]     <- -S * K * dxi[, "log10G"]   J[, "log10Ha"]    <- -S * K * (dxi[, "log10Ha"] + ln10 * Ha * viaRest(eqm$dHa))   J[, "log10TauK"]  <- -S * K * dxi[, "log10TauK"]   J[, "log10S"]     <-  ln10 * prec   J[, "logit10K"]   <- -S * (xi + K * dxi[, "K"]) * ln10 * K * (1 - K)   J[, "logit10Phi"] <- -S * K * viaRest(eqm$dPhi) * pi / 2 * ln10 * u * (1 - u)   J[, bn[1]] <- ln10 * e1   J[, bn[2]] <- ln10 * e1 * tt / T1   J[, bn[3]] <- ln10 * e2   J[, bn[4]] <- ln10 * e2 * tt / T2   list(y = e1 + e2 + prec, J = J) }  likelihood <- function(p) {               # innovations: the whitened residuals   r <- J <- innovations <- vector("list", length(fields))   for (k in seq_along(fields)) {     part <- traceSignal(p, k, obs[[k]]$time_ps)     if (is.null(part)) return(NULL)     sn <- sigmaName(fields[k])     z  <- maResiduals(part$y - obs[[k]]$signal, part$J, p[[sn]], p[kernel])     if (is.null(z)) return(NULL)     z$J[, sn]     <- z$dSigma     z$J[, kernel] <- z$dW     r[[k]] <- z$r     J[[k]] <- z$J     innovations[[k]] <- z$r[seq_along(part$y)]   }   list(r = unlist(r), J = do.call(rbind, J),        innovations = setNames(innovations, paste(fields, "kOe"))) }  priorSd   <- 3 prior     <- c(log10Alpha = -1, log10G = log10(2), log10Ha = 3,                log10TauK = log10(30), log10S = 0, logit10K = 0,                logit10Phi = log10(0.5)) residuals <- withPrior(likelihood, prior, priorSd)

title: 4. Reverse mode
text: derivMode cppODE() selects derivatives model returns: "forward" (default) tangent, "reverse" cotangent, "forward-reverse" cotangent together tangent curvature, "forward-forward" (deriv2 = TRUE) Hessian every state. chapter compares reverse builds decay chain forward-forward build.
code: eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B") parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2) times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)  fwd  <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "forward-forward", modelname = "g4_fwd", compile = FALSE) rev  <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", modelname = "g4_rev", compile = FALSE) fr   <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "forward-reverse", modelname = "g4_fr", compile = FALSE) fast <- cppODE(c(x = "-k*x + sin(100*time)*q"), derivMode = "reverse",                modelname = "g4_fast", compile = FALSE)  compile(fwd, rev, fr, fast, output = "guide4", cores = 2)

title: 4. Reverse mode
text: reverse model takes cotangent \(w\) shape [time, state] solveODE() returns $cotangent, gradient \[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \sum_{t, } w_{t,}\, x_i(t)\] initial values parameters \(\theta\), one row . cotangent single non-zero entry gives one row sensitivity matrix. third dimension holds several seeds, swept back together one forward pass; $cotangent one column per seed.
code: w <- matrix(0, length(times), 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"))) w[101, "B"] <- 1 outR <- solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = w) outR$cotangent #>          [,1] #> A   0.2143297 #> B   0.1353352 #> k1 -0.1734723 #> k2 -1.5411580  outF <- solveODE(fwd, times, parms) outF$tangent[101, "B", ]                # ∂B(10)/∂θ from forward mode #>          A          B         k1         k2  #>  0.2143280  0.1353353 -0.1734757 -1.5411625 outR$cotangent[, 1] - solveODE(fwd, times, parms, sensErrCon = FALSE)$tangent[101, "B", ] #>             A             B            k1            k2  #> -2.775558e-17  1.110223e-16  1.665335e-16  8.881784e-16 W <- array(0, c(length(times), 2, 2),            dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"), c("A10", "B10"))) W[101, "A", "A10"] <- 1 W[101, "B", "B10"] <- 1 solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = W)$cotangent #>             A10        B10 #> A   0.006737421  0.2143297 #> B   0.000000000  0.1353352 #> k1 -0.067380395 -0.1734723 #> k2  0.000000000 -1.5411580

title: 4. Reverse mode
text: \(L = \sum_t (B(t) - y_t)^2\) cotangent \(\partial L / \partial B(t) = 2\,(B(t) - y_t)\). depends solution, forward pass runs first: keepStore = TRUE cotangent, solveODE() returns values keeps checkpoints $store. solve given store times parms integrates nothing runs backward sweep alone. store may reused number cotangents freed next garbage collection, count checkpoint memory. releaseStore() frees ; solve given released store integrates .
code: y   <- 0.4 * exp(-0.3 * times) * (1 - exp(-times)) first <- solveODE(rev, times, parms, keepStore = TRUE) res <- first$variable[, "B"] - y  wL <- cbind(A = 0, B = 2 * res) grad <- solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = wL, store = first$store)$cotangent cbind(reverse = grad[, 1], forward = 2 * colSums(res * outF$tangent[, "B", ])) #>       reverse   forward #> A   25.009083  25.00933 #> B   23.696642  23.69663 #> k1   7.042661   7.04377 #> k2 -74.693071 -74.69188 releaseStore(first$store)

title: 4. Reverse mode
text: default sweep runs step grid forward pass. grid resolves states need resolve derivatives: \(\dot x = -k x + \sin(100\, t)\, q\) \(q = 0\) state smooth \(\partial x/\partial q\) follows fast forcing, exact gradient \(\sum_t x(t)\) \(q\) closed form. Tighter tolerances reduce error sweep without removing , since states set grid. adjointControl(), passed adjoint, sets sweep: refine = TRUE holds step reltol abstol sweeps failing step substeps, gradtol adds absolute tolerance contribution step gradient, trace = TRUE returns grid $adjoint (Grid refinement sweep). refined sweep differentiates slightly different trajectory one forward pass computed. $correction first-order change seeded functional two, value plus correction value whose gradient $cotangent (value correction). $adjoint holds time h every step sweep, adjoint state lambda step start, refine substeps failures per step.
code: tf <- seq(0, 2, by = 0.1) pf <- c(x = 1, k = 1, q = 0) Wf <- cbind(x = rep(1, length(tf))) exact <- sum((sin(100*tf) - 100*cos(100*tf) + 100*exp(-tf)) / 10001)  val <- solveODE(fast, tf, pf, cotangent = Wf) tgt <- solveODE(fast, tf, pf, cotangent = Wf, abstol = 1e-12, reltol = 1e-12) chk <- solveODE(fast, tf, pf, cotangent = Wf,                 adjoint = adjointControl(refine = TRUE, gradtol = 1e-9, trace = TRUE)) c(exact = exact, valueGrid = val$cotangent[["q", 1]], tight = tgt$cotangent[["q", 1]],   refined = chk$cotangent[["q", 1]]) #>      exact  valueGrid      tight    refined  #> 0.08342800 1.77299898 0.14264118 0.08366032 c(steps = length(chk$adjoint$h), substeps = sum(chk$adjoint$substeps)) #>    steps substeps  #>       35     2104 chk$correction #> [1] 0.0001015525 ggplot(data.frame(time = chk$adjoint$time, substeps = chk$adjoint$substeps),        aes(time, substeps)) +   geom_step() +   scale_y_log10()

title: 4. Reverse mode
text: derivMode = "forward-reverse" differentiates sweep along tangent (forward reverse). Besides $tangent $cotangent returns $curvature, [state parameter, direction, seed], derivative $cotangent along tangent direction: default identity tangent, Hessian seeded functional. cotangent depends solution, \(2\,(B - y)\), passes cotangent derivative along tangent argument curvature, [time, state, seed, direction], \(2\,\partial B / \partial \theta\); without Hessian misses term, gradient . Hessian forward-forward model, Gauss-Newton term plus residual term: first call computes residual tangent, cotangent serves . keepStore reverse-option, forward-reverse objective solves twice. tangent fewer columns gives Hessian-vector products, product \(v = (0, 0, 1, -1)\): sensErrCon = TRUE (default) includes tangents error test forward pass; FALSE gives step grid depend directions.
code: first <- solveODE(fr, times, parms, cotangent = wL) res   <- first$variable[, "B"] - y wL    <- cbind(A = 0, B = 2 * res)  cv <- array(0, c(length(times), 2, 1, 4), dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"), NULL, NULL)) cv[, "B", 1, ] <- 2 * first$tangent[, "B", ] outFR <- solveODE(fr, times, parms, cotangent = wL, curvature = cv) H <- outFR$curvature[, , 1] H #>      sens #> theta          A          B        k1         k2 #>    A    33.35838   34.25193  19.61416 -166.85157 #>    B    34.25193   50.10908  21.84923 -170.19220 #>    k1   19.61416   21.84923 -24.36330  -45.21293 #>    k2 -166.85157 -170.19220 -45.21293  678.74552 S  <- outF$tangent[, "B", ] H2 <- 2 * crossprod(S) + 2 * apply(res * outF$hessian[, "B", , ], c(2, 3), sum) max(abs(H - H2)) #> [1] 2.273737e-13 v  <- matrix(c(0, 0, 1, -1), 4, 1, dimnames = list(names(parms), "v")) cv <- array(0, c(length(times), 2, 1, 1), dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"), NULL, NULL)) cv[, "B", 1, 1] <- 2 * first$tangent[, "B", ] %*% v Hv <- solveODE(fr, times, parms, tangent = v, cotangent = wL, curvature = cv)$curvature[, , 1] cbind(Hv, H %*% v) #>            Hv          v #> A   186.46567  186.46574 #> B   192.04143  192.04143 #> k1   20.84937   20.84963 #> k2 -723.95861 -723.95845

title: 3. Sensitivities
text: tangent solveODE() Jacobian \(\partial(x_0, p)/\partial\theta\) reparametrization. result \(\partial x/\partial\theta\), one column per direction, cost grows number columns. Three shapes told apart rows: partial tangent unit vectors k1 k2 gives reduced sensitivities, single column directional derivative. two directional results agree integration tolerance: step grid follows tangent, see sensErrCon. full tangent rate constants log scale, \(k_i = e^{\theta_i}\), column \(\partial k_i/\partial \theta_i = k_i\).  state-tangent shape $tangent[t, , ], one solve continues another, sensitivities included. chain autonomous, two solves five time units agree one ten integration tolerance.
code: S <- diag(2) dimnames(S) <- list(c("k1", "k2"), c("k1", "k2")) solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = S)$tangent[101, , ] #>         sens #> variable          k1        k2 #>        A -0.06737644  0.000000 #>        B -0.17347569 -1.541163  v <- matrix(c(1, -1), 2, dimnames = list(c("k1", "k2"), "k1 - k2")) solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = v)$tangent[101, , "k1 - k2"] #>           A           B  #> -0.06737592  1.36768749 out$tangent[101, , "k1"] - out$tangent[101, , "k2"] #>           A           B  #> -0.06737644  1.36768686 Tlog <- rbind(matrix(0, 2, 2), diag(parms[c("k1", "k2")])) dimnames(Tlog) <- list(names(parms), c("log_k1", "log_k2")) outL <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = Tlog)  ggplot(longFormat(outL, "B"), aes(time, value)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +   scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) first <- solveODE(chain, seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), parms) x5    <- first$variable[51, ] then  <- solveODE(chain, seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), c(x5, parms[c("k1", "k2")]),                   tangent = first$tangent[51, , ]) max(abs(then$tangent[51, , ] - out$tangent[101, , ])) #> [1] 5.918106e-06

title: 5. Steady states
text: decay chain production k0 \(\) steady state \(= k_0/k_1\), \(B = k_0/k_2\). rootfunc cppODE() ends integration: "equilibrate" steady state, vector expressions first zero . ptc() takes cppFUN() object forward derivatives, right-hand sides enzyme \(E + S \rightleftharpoons ES \E + P\) \(P \S\), bistable switch.
code: eqns  <- c(A = "k0 - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B") parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k0 = 1, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)  steady <- cppODE(eqns, rootfunc = "equilibrate", modelname = "g5_steady", compile = FALSE) cross  <- cppODE(eqns, rootfunc = "A - B", modelname = "g5_cross", compile = FALSE)  enzyme <- c(E  = "-kon*E*S + (koff + kcat)*ES",             S  = "-kon*E*S + koff*ES + kback*P",             ES = " kon*E*S - (koff + kcat)*ES",             P  = " kcat*ES - kback*P") enz <- cppFUN(enzyme, variables = names(enzyme),               parameters = c("kon", "koff", "kcat", "kback"), modelname = "g5_enzyme") switch1 <- cppFUN(c(x = "a + b*x^2/(1 + x^2) - x"), variables = "x",                   parameters = c("a", "b"), modelname = "g5_switch")  compile(steady, cross, enz, switch1, output = "guide5", cores = 2)

title: Sensitivities across events, checked symbolically
text: One dsolve() per smooth segment, pinned state segment start glued next segment firing time.
code: sym  <- function(name, ...) sp$Symbol(name, real = TRUE, ...) tSym <- sym("t")  # Integer exponents only. A float power blocks the simplifications that # turn the solution of an oscillator back into a sine. pow <- function(base, exponent) sp$Pow(base, as.integer(exponent))  # One smooth segment of a first order equation, pinned by y(t0) = y0. segment <- function(fun, rhs, t0, y0)   sp$dsolve(sp$Eq(sp$Derivative(fun(tSym), tSym), rhs), fun(tSym),             ics = reticulate::py_dict(list(fun(t0)), list(y0)))$rhs  # The same for a second order equation, pinned by y(t0) and y'(t0). segment2 <- function(fun, rhs, t0, y0, dy0)   sp$dsolve(sp$Eq(sp$Derivative(fun(tSym), tSym, 2L), rhs), fun(tSym),             ics = reticulate::py_dict(               list(fun(t0), sp$Derivative(fun(tSym), tSym)$subs(tSym, t0)),               list(y0, dy0)))$rhs  # Segments glued at their firing times, one branch longer than fires. composed <- function(branches, fires) {   pieces <- Map(function(branch, fire) reticulate::tuple(branch, sp$Lt(tSym, fire)),                 branches[seq_along(fires)], fires)   do.call(sp$Piecewise,           c(pieces, list(reticulate::tuple(branches[[length(branches)]], sp$`true`)))) }  # A parameter point: the symbols, their values, and the grid to compare on. # The names are the ones solveODE() labels the sensitivity slices with, where # a state name stands for that state's initial value. point <- function(syms, pars, times)   list(syms = syms, names = names(pars), values = as.list(unname(pars)),        times = times)  toNumeric <- function(expr)   suppressWarnings(as.numeric(reticulate::py_str(sp$N(expr))))  # Every parameter replaced by the value at the point, time left free. atPoint <- function(expr, at) expr$subs(reticulate::py_dict(at$syms, at$values))  # SymPy's lambdify reads the frame of the caller for a docstring and a call from R # has none, so it goes through a Python function. Compiling once per expression # turns one round trip per time point into one per panel. sympyGrid <- reticulate::py_run_string( "import sympy def over_grid(sym, expr, grid):     f = sympy.lambdify(sym, expr, 'math')     return [f(v) for v in grid] ")  # The expression, or a derivative of it, over the whole time grid. A constant # expression still yields one value per time point. series <- function(expr, at, wrt = list()) {   for (s in wrt) expr <- sp$diff(expr, s)   as.numeric(sympyGrid$over_grid(tSym, atPoint(expr, at), at$times)) }  # Numeric value of an expression that no longer depends on time. value <- function(expr, at) toNumeric(atPoint(expr, at))  # The first zero after `after`, over one condition or several at once, picked # numerically among the symbolic roots. Complex branches drop out as NA. crossing <- function(conditions, at, after = 0) {   if (!is.list(conditions)) conditions <- list(conditions)   roots <- unlist(lapply(conditions,                          function(g) sp$solve(sp$Eq(g, sp$Integer(0L)), tSym)),                   recursive = FALSE)   when <- vapply(roots, value, 0, at = at)   roots[[which.min(ifelse(!is.na(when) & when > after + 1e-9, when, Inf))]] }

title: Sensitivities across events, checked symbolically
text: comparison() pairs symbolic forward derivatives, reverseSeries() adds forward reverse, report() prints largest differences per order, comparisonPlot() draws .
code:
# Panel labels use the partial derivative sign, U+2202. lab1 <- function(var, a) sprintf("∂%s / ∂%s", var, a) lab2 <- function(var, a, b) {   if (a == b) return(sprintf("∂²%s / ∂%s²", var, a))   sprintf("∂²%s / ∂%s∂%s", var, a, b) }  # The last row at a requested time holds the post-event state, whether # or not a localized root inserted extra rows. rowsAt <- function(res, times)   vapply(times, function(s) max(which(abs(res$time - s) < 1e-9)), 1L)  # One panel per quantity: the state, the gradient, and each distinct # second derivative, symbolic against what solveODE() returned. comparison <- function(expr, at, res, var) {   i  <- rowsAt(res, at$times)   np <- length(at$syms)    # One entry per panel, each holding both curves over the whole grid.   panel <- function(order, quantity, symbolic, numeric)     list(order = order, quantity = quantity,          symbolic = symbolic, numeric = as.numeric(numeric))    panels <- list(panel(0L, var, series(expr, at), res$variable[i, var]))   for (a in seq_len(np))     panels[[length(panels) + 1L]] <-       panel(1L, lab1(var, at$names[a]), series(expr, at, at$syms[a]),             res$tangent[i, var, at$names[a]])   for (a in seq_len(np)) for (b in a:np)     panels[[length(panels) + 1L]] <-       panel(2L, lab2(var, at$names[a], at$names[b]),             series(expr, at, at$syms[c(a, b)]),             res$hessian[i, var, at$names[a], at$names[b]])    labels <- vapply(panels, `[[`, "", "quantity")   data.frame(     order    = rep(vapply(panels, `[[`, 0L, "order"), each = length(at$times)),     quantity = factor(rep(labels, each = length(at$times)), levels = labels),     time     = rep(at$times, length(panels)),     symbolic = unlist(lapply(panels, `[[`, "symbolic"), use.names = FALSE),     numeric  = unlist(lapply(panels, `[[`, "numeric"), use.names = FALSE)) }  # The numeric side of the figures, one line per derivative order. report <- function(df, title) {   cat("
", title, "
", sep = "")   for (o in sort(unique(df$order))) {     d <- df[df$order == o, ]     cat(sprintf("  %-13s max |solveODE - symbolic| = %.2e
",                 c("state", "first order", "second order")[o + 1L],                 max(abs(d$numeric - d$symbolic))))   } }  # Forward over reverse at every `every`-th output time: a cotangent seeded on # one row and state makes the gradient that state's row of the tangent and the # curvature the Hessian of that state. Only requested times are seeded, since a row a root # inserts moves with the parameters. reverseSeries <- function(expr, at, res, model, pars, var, states,                           opts = list(), every = 50L) {   keep <- seq(1L, length(at$times), by = every)   i    <- rowsAt(res, at$times)[keep]   W    <- array(0, c(nrow(res$variable), length(states), length(keep)))   for (r in seq_along(keep)) W[i[r], match(var, states), r] <- 1   rev <- do.call(solveODE, c(list(model, at$times, pars, cotangent = W), opts))    np  <- length(at$syms)   out <- list()   add <- function(order, quantity, symbolic, numeric)     out[[length(out) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(       order = order, quantity = quantity, time = at$times[keep],       symbolic = symbolic, reverse = as.numeric(numeric))    for (a in seq_len(np))     add(1L, lab1(var, at$names[a]),         series(expr, at, at$syms[a])[keep], rev$cotangent[at$names[a], ])   for (a in seq_len(np)) for (b in a:np)     add(2L, lab2(var, at$names[a], at$names[b]),         series(expr, at, at$syms[c(a, b)])[keep],         rev$curvature[at$names[a], at$names[b], ])    df <- do.call(rbind, out)   for (o in 1:2) {     d <- df[df$order == o, ]     cat(sprintf("  %-13s max |reverse - symbolic| = %.2e
",                 c("reverse 1st", "reverse 2nd")[o],                 max(abs(d$reverse - d$symbolic))))   }   df }  # `rev` draws forward over reverse on top, one point per seeded row. comparisonPlot <- function(df, orders, title, rev = NULL) {   p <- ggplot(df[df$order %in% orders, ], aes(x = time)) +     # A quantity that vanishes identically leaves the solver a cancellation     # residue of a few ulp, and a free y scale would blow that up into a     # picture of the round-off. No panel is drawn tighter than this.     expand_limits(y = c(-1e-10, 1e-10)) +     geom_line(aes(y = symbolic, color = "symbolic", linetype = "symbolic"),               linewidth = 1) +     geom_line(aes(y = numeric, color = "forward", linetype = "forward"),               linewidth = 1)   if (!is.null(rev)) {     rev$quantity <- factor(rev$quantity, levels = levels(df$quantity))     p <- p + geom_point(data = rev[rev$order %in% orders, ],                         aes(y = reverse, color = "reverse"),                         shape = 21, fill = NA)   }   p + facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +     scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +     scale_color_manual(values = c(symbolic = "#000000", forward = "#E69F00", reverse = "#0072B2"),                        breaks = c("symbolic", "forward", "reverse")) +     scale_linetype_manual(values = c(symbolic = "solid", forward = "dotdash"), guide = "none") +     guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = c("solid", "dotdash", "blank"),                                                     shape = c(NA, NA, 21)))) +     labs(title = title, x = "time", y = NULL, color = NULL) +     theme(legend.position = "top") }

code: events_pair <- data.frame(var = "C", time = NA, value = "d", method = "add",                           root = "S - c", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) model_pair  <- cppODE(c(S = "a", C = "-b * C"), events = events_pair,                       deriv = TRUE, deriv2 = TRUE, modelname = "saltation_pair")  pars_pair  <- c(S = 2, C = 4, a = 1, b = 0.1, c = 14, d = 3) times_pair <- seq(0, 20, len = 1000) # Tight tolerances throughout, so what is left of the residual is the solver # and not the saltation transport. roottol matters as much: the firing time # enters the state through the velocity, so a loose root is a state error. res_pair <- solveODE(model_pair, times_pair, pars_pair,                      abstol = 1e-12, reltol = 1e-12, roottol = 1e-12)  S0 <- sym("S0"); C0 <- sym("C0"); a <- sym("a") b  <- sym("b");  cc <- sym("c");  d <- sym("d") Sfun <- sp$Function("S"); Cfun <- sp$Function("C")  point_pair <- point(list(S0, C0, a, b, cc, d),                     pars_pair[c("S", "C", "a", "b", "c", "d")], times_pair) S_of_t <- segment(Sfun, a, sp$Integer(0L), S0) fire_pair <- crossing(S_of_t - cc, point_pair) C_before  <- segment(Cfun, -b * Cfun(tSym), sp$Integer(0L), C0) C_after   <- segment(Cfun, -b * Cfun(tSym), fire_pair,                      C_before$subs(tSym, fire_pair) + d) C_of_t    <- composed(list(C_before, C_after), list(fire_pair))  cmp_pair <- comparison(C_of_t, point_pair, res_pair, "C") model_pair_r <- cppODE(c(S = "a", C = "-b * C"), events = events_pair,                        derivMode = "forward-reverse", modelname = "saltation_pair_r") rev_pair <- reverseSeries(C_of_t, point_pair, res_pair, model_pair_r, pars_pair,                           "C", c("S", "C"),                           opts = list(abstol = 1e-12, reltol = 1e-12,                                       roottol = 1e-12)) #> Warning: saltation/pair.rds was computed from other code or another cppDE #> version; delete it to compute it again report(cmp_pair, "root event on a coupled pair") #>  #> root event on a coupled pair #>   state         max |solveODE - symbolic| = 2.24e-11 #>   first order   max |solveODE - symbolic| = 1.01e-09 #>   second order  max |solveODE - symbolic| = 3.64e-08 plot_pair_1 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_pair, 0:1, "C and gradient across a root event",                               rev_pair) plot_pair_1 plot_pair_2 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_pair, 2L, "Second derivatives of C across a root event",                               rev_pair) plot_pair_2

code: events_wall <- data.frame(var = c("v", "v"), time = c(NA, NA),                           value = c("-1", "-1"),                           method = c("multiply", "multiply"),                           root = c("x - L", "x + L"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) model_wall  <- cppODE(c(x = "v", v = "-w^2 * x"), events = events_wall,                       deriv = TRUE, deriv2 = TRUE, modelname = "saltation_wall") model_wall_r <- cppODE(c(x = "v", v = "-w^2 * x"), events = events_wall,                        derivMode = "forward-reverse",                        modelname = "saltation_wall_r")  pars_wall  <- c(x = 0.2, v = 1.2, w = 1, L = 0.8) times_wall <- seq(0, 11, len = 1000) # Two firings per wall, so 8 bounces before the grid ends. res_wall <- solveODE(model_wall, times_wall, pars_wall, maxroot = 4L,                      abstol = 1e-12, reltol = 1e-12, roottol = 1e-12)  x_ini <- sym("x0"); v_ini <- sym("v0") freq  <- sp$Symbol("w", real = TRUE, positive = TRUE) wall  <- sp$Symbol("L", real = TRUE, positive = TRUE)  point_wall <- point(list(x_ini, v_ini, freq, wall),                     pars_wall[c("x", "v", "w", "L")], times_wall) oscillation <- function(t0, y0, dy0)   segment2(xfun, -pow(freq, 2) * xfun(tSym), t0, y0, dy0)  # From the initial state to whichever wall comes first. approach   <- oscillation(sp$Integer(0L), x_ini, v_ini) first_hit  <- crossing(list(approach - wall, approach + wall), point_wall) first_side <- sign(value(approach$subs(tSym, first_hit), point_wall))  # The energy survives the reflection, so every flight between the walls is one # arc up to a sign and a time shift. Solved once it stays small, while composing # it bounce by bounce through dsolve() nests one inverse tangent per wall. energy <- sp$simplify(pow(sp$diff(approach, tSym), 2) + pow(freq, 2) * pow(approach, 2)) speed  <- sp$sqrt(energy - pow(freq, 2) * pow(wall, 2)) stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(   value(speed, point_wall),   first_side * value(sp$diff(approach, tSym)$subs(tSym, first_hit), point_wall))))  # One arc, from the wall it leaves to the opposite one, in the time since # that bounce. flight_arc  <- oscillation(sp$Integer(0L), wall, -speed) flight_time <- crossing(flight_arc + wall, point_wall)  branches_wall <- list(approach) fires_wall    <- list(first_hit) side          <- first_side for (j in 1:8) {   branches_wall[[j + 1]] <- sp$Integer(as.integer(side)) *     flight_arc$subs(tSym, tSym - fires_wall[[j]])   if (j < 8) fires_wall[[j + 1]] <- fires_wall[[j]] + flight_time   side <- -side } x_wall <- composed(branches_wall, fires_wall) v_wall <- sp$diff(x_wall, tSym)  cmp_wall_x <- comparison(x_wall, point_wall, res_wall, "x") cmp_wall_v <- comparison(v_wall, point_wall, res_wall, "v") rev_wall_x <- reverseSeries(x_wall, point_wall, res_wall, model_wall_r,                             pars_wall, "x", c("x", "v"),                             opts = list(maxroot = 4L, abstol = 1e-12,                                         reltol = 1e-12, roottol = 1e-12)) rev_wall_v <- reverseSeries(v_wall, point_wall, res_wall, model_wall_r,                             pars_wall, "v", c("x", "v"),                             opts = list(maxroot = 4L, abstol = 1e-12,                                         reltol = 1e-12, roottol = 1e-12)) #> Warning: saltation/wall.rds was computed from other code or another cppDE #> version; delete it to compute it again report(cmp_wall_x, "oscillator between elastic walls, position") #>  #> oscillator between elastic walls, position #>   state         max |solveODE - symbolic| = 3.92e-10 #>   first order   max |solveODE - symbolic| = 5.17e-09 #>   second order  max |solveODE - symbolic| = 1.31e-07 report(cmp_wall_v, "oscillator between elastic walls, velocity") #>  #> oscillator between elastic walls, velocity #>   state         max |solveODE - symbolic| = 3.40e-10 #>   first order   max |solveODE - symbolic| = 7.17e-09 #>   second order  max |solveODE - symbolic| = 7.03e-08 plot_wall_1 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_wall_x, 0:1, "Position and gradient over 8 bounces",                               rev_wall_x) plot_wall_1 plot_wall_2 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_wall_x, 2L, "Second derivatives of the position",                               rev_wall_x) plot_wall_2 plot_wall_3 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_wall_v, 0:1, "Velocity and gradient over 8 bounces",                               rev_wall_v) plot_wall_3 plot_wall_4 <- comparisonPlot(cmp_wall_v, 2L, "Second derivatives of the velocity",                               rev_wall_v) plot_wall_4

code: # \donttest{ if (codegenAvailable()) {   ## Six variants of one decay chain A -> B. Each is generated first and all   ## are compiled together afterwards, into one shared object in tempdir().   eqns <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")    ## First-order sensitivities, the default   fwd <- cppODE(eqns, compile = FALSE)    ## A dose of A at the parameter time t_e   events <- data.frame(var = "A", time = "t_e", value = 1, method = "add")   dosed  <- cppODE(eqns, events = events, compile = FALSE)    ## A constant inflow k0, integrated until the steady state   steady <- cppODE(c(A = "k0 - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B"),                    rootfunc = "equilibrate", compile = FALSE)    ## A time-dependent input u, given as data when solving   forced <- cppODE(c(A = "u - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B"), forcings = "u",                    compile = FALSE)    ## Second-order sensitivities   fwd2 <- cppODE(eqns, deriv2 = TRUE, compile = FALSE)    ## Reverse mode: the states in plain double, the derivatives from one   ## backward sweep whose cost does not grow with the number of parameters   rev <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", compile = FALSE)    compile(fwd, dosed, steady, forced, fwd2, rev, output = "cppODE_examples")    times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.5)   parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)    out <- solveODE(fwd, times, parms)   head(out$variable)   out$tangent[21, "B", ]                # dB(10) / d(A, B, k1, k2)    out <- solveODE(dosed, times, c(parms, t_e = 4))   out$variable[times %in% c(3.5, 4, 4.5), ]    out <- solveODE(steady, times = c(0, 1000), c(parms, k0 = 1))   tail(out$time, 1)                     # stopped before t = 1000   tail(out$variable, 1)                 # the steady state    u   <- list(u = data.frame(time = times, value = 1 + sin(times)))   out <- solveODE(forced, times, parms, forcings = u)   out$variable[21, ]    out <- solveODE(fwd2, times, parms)   out$hessian[21, "B", , ]              # Hessian of B(10)    ## The gradient of sum(B) over the grid: a cotangent of ones on B   onB <- cbind(A = 0, B = rep(1, length(times)))   solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = onB)$cotangent } # }
